service.name: After-party entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music and DJs for conference after-parties, gala after-parties and corporate late nights
service.description: After-party entertainment for conferences, galas and company parties in Denver and across Colorado: open-format DJ with a live musician, live band karaoke, soul and R&B band and yacht rock band, on one contract with the venue's load-in window and sound cap settled before the day.

faqs.q: Can the after-party start the moment the program ends?
faqs.a: Yes. The sound system goes up before the doors open, so the band or the DJ is set and checked during the reception, can play dinner quietly if the night wants it, and starts the dance floor on the emcee's last word, with no changeover the guests can see.

faqs.q: Do we need a second sound system for the after-party?
faqs.a: No. Sound support that's the right size for the venue is included, and a band, the DJ and a live musician over the DJ set all run through it on the same contract. A hotel's house system is built for speeches and won't carry a dance floor across a ballroom, which is why ours comes with the booking.

faqs.q: What does the hotel need to know?
faqs.a: The dock time and the elevator window, one or two dedicated 20-amp circuits depending on the act, the sound cap and the curfew, and the run of show. Setup runs 45 to 90 minutes depending on the size of the act, and a certificate of insurance, the W-9 and one itemized invoice come with the contract. We settle all of it with the events office before the day.
Yes. The DJ reads the floor from the first song and builds an open-format set for a crowd from six cities, and live band karaoke takes requests by definition.

faqs.q: How loud can it be, and what about the curfew?
faqs.a: As loud as a dance floor wants and the venue allows. Give us the hotel's sound cap and curfew when we sign, and the set is built under them from the start, so nobody has to turn it down on the night. The downtown hotels and the convention-center properties each run their own rules, and we settle them with the events office.
